brief: Cboe's weekly note reports the VIX gained over 16pts week over week to a 1-year high of 36% in Friday's selloff, but attributes most of the move to idiosyncratic risk rather than macro risk: equity vol far outpaced other asset classes on a z-score basis. The SPX's -3.7% spot drop and a 3.2pt rise in fixed-strike vols drove almost 90% of the 7.4pt VIX increase; skew and convexity added just 0.9pt, versus nearly half of the Nov 5th spike, and call skew/convexity showed no rush into upside calls. The note calls the move orderly, with no panic, but also no positioning for a quick rebound. Single-stock vol (VIXEQSM) rose to a 1-year high of 58%, more than index vol, and dispersion (DSPXSM) rose 5pts, consistent with rotation out of AI names into other sectors rather than indiscriminate selling. QQQ implied vol jumped over 20pts, the most of any global index, while small-cap (RTY) vol trailed, narrowing the RTY-SPX spread to a 6-year low of 1.4%. Bonds rallied, credit and rate vol rose moderately, and commodities fell, led by gold (-9%), whose implied vol is the richest cross-asset vol, near 3 standard deviations above average.
